assumptions: source assumption: fixed problem size (page: serial fraction diagnoses scaling for a problem of fixed size).
S is measured speedup psi = T(1)/T(p) on the same workload and code version as the serial-fraction claim.
application profile: N identical processors with the parallel work evenly distributable; load imbalance and overhead surface inside e rather than as separate terms.

gaps: Meanings experimental_serial_fraction/measured_speedup/processor_count absent from runtime vocabulary; scalar form fits engine once meanings exist.
No verified distinct calibration of this metric against Amdahl/Gustafson records; cross-record consistency noted only.

models.inverse_notes: N = (1-e)/(1/S - e) needs 1/S != e; S = 1/(e + (1-e)/N) needs nonzero denominator. Check: e=0.2,N=16 gives S = 1/(0.2+0.05) = 4. Algebraic inversion only, not causal; e outside [0,1] can arise under overhead/superlinear effects and is diagnostic, not rejected.
limitations: Source page states this is a diagnostic metric consistent with Amdahl, not a derivation from it; Amdahl ignores load balance and overhead, which is exactly what e is meant to expose.
Source article carries a March-2020 lacking-inline-citations notice; the underlying paper (Karp & Flatt 1990, CACM 33(5):539-543) is cited by the page but was not directly inspected.
Fixed-size problems only; scaled-workload (Gustafson) diagnosis needs a separate treatment.

references.method: Amdahl-consistency substitution from the source justification: 1/psi = e + (1-e)/p gives 0.2 + 0.8/16 = 0.25 = 1/4. Exact decimal; tolerance covers float division.
references.provenance: Independent derivation via the source's Amdahl-consistency equation.

references.method: Limiting identity: ideal linear speedup implies zero experimentally determined serial fraction.
Fully serial limit: (1 - 1/8)/(1 - 1/8) = 1; no speedup on 8 processors implies unit serial fraction.

rejection_cases.reason: N = 1 makes the denominator 1 - 1/N zero; source requires p > 1 (metric undefined for uniprocessor).
Measured speedup S is required alongside N; omitting it leaves e undetermined.

relationship.locator: Description section: metric definition e = ((1/psi) - (1/p)) / (1 - (1/p)) with p > 1; Justification section derives the equivalent 1/psi = e + (1-e)/p form.
relationship.translation_notes: Source symbols psi -> S (measured speedup), p -> N (processor count), e -> e. Denominator exclusion N != 1 preserved as guard N > 1 per source p > 1. Check: dimensionless ratio arithmetic.

sources.evidence: Defines the experimentally determined serial fraction e from measured speedup psi on p > 1 processors via the stated quotient, shows consistency with Amdahl through 1/psi = e + (1-e)/p, and cites Karp & Flatt 1990 CACM 33(5):539-543 (paper not directly inspected; article lacks inline citations per its March-2020 notice).
